items.text: Producer identity. Is every status, check or comment trusted only from the expected App, bot or login? (Not by name; a newer "success" from another app must not count.)
Present vs absent. Does a missing required signal (check, status, hold, record) refuse, rather than count as "nothing blocking"?
Ordering. Is it ordered by id or sequence, never by created_at or timestamps (missing, invalid or equal timestamps)?
Read-then-write races. Is there a re-read after every write, fail-closed if anything changed or appeared (concurrent holds, other hosts)?
Head binding. Is every decision pinned to an exact 40-hex head, re-verified right before and after the write, with refusal on a moved head?
Binding to the round or run. Can a hold or success from one round or run clear another? Bind to an id; refuse unbound.
Fail-open catches. Does any try/catch, default value or "unknown" path end in allow? Every unreadable input must refuse.
Write ordering. Is dedupe or state persisted only AFTER the effect succeeds (no suppressed retries)?
Crash windows. If the process dies between steps, which state is left? Never leave a gate open; post a pending hold first and success last.
Credentials. Which token writes? Never fall back to personal credentials; refuse without the App token.
Environment hardening. Are GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, replace objects, grafts, commit-graph, PATH and credential helpers controlled? Fetches must verify the fetched sha.
Scope of exemptions. Does any skip or no-op rule trust a label or policy string without re-deriving it from the diff?
Process liveness. Can a surviving child or uid process change files after a verdict is recorded? Then the verdict must not be trusted.
Simplest correct option. Before adding machinery (retries, markers, carry), is there a stateless alternative (e.g. update-branch → fresh round)? Prefer it.
